lines.text: In nineteen eleven, a man stole the Mona Lisa from the Louvre.
The police searched for over two years.
But here's the unbelievable part: they actually questioned the thief... while the painting was hidden inside his apartment.
Paris, August nineteen eleven.
The Louvre was one of Europe's great museums.
Inside hung Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa.
It was already admired by art lovers, but almost nobody expected what was about to happen.
His name was Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian worker who had previously worked at the museum.
He knew its galleries and was familiar with the building.
And on August twenty-first, the painting vanished.
The next day, painter Louis Béroud arrived at the Louvre.
He expected to see the Mona Lisa hanging in its usual place.
Instead, he found an empty space.
At first, people thought it had simply been moved.
But when museum officials realized it was truly missing, Paris erupted in disbelief.
Newspapers spread the story across the world.
People even visited the Louvre just to stare at the empty wall.
Investigators followed leads and questioned people connected to the art world.
Even Pablo Picasso was questioned.
Yet the painting remained missing.
One of the biggest mysteries in art history had begun.
Meanwhile, Peruggia was living in Paris.
Investigators had even interviewed him, but accepted his explanation.
They didn't realize the stolen masterpiece was still hidden inside his apartment.
Months became years.
The Mona Lisa stayed hidden while the mystery grew.
Then, in late nineteen thirteen, Peruggia contacted an art dealer in Florence.
He claimed he wanted to return the painting to Italy.
The dealer, Alfredo Geri, contacted the director of the Uffizi Gallery.
They examined the painting and recognized it as the missing masterpiece.
The authorities were alerted.
Peruggia's secret was finally exposed.
After more than two years, the Mona Lisa was finally recovered.
In January nineteen fourteen, it returned to the Louvre.
The theft had transformed an admired Renaissance painting into a worldwide celebrity.
Today, the Mona Lisa is one of the world's most recognizable paintings.
And its greatest publicity came from the man who stole it.
So here's the question: did the thief accidentally make it famous?
